original_query: select    min(s_store_name)   ,min(s_company_id)   ,min(s_street_number)   ,min(s_street_name)   ,min(s_suite_number)   ,min(s_city)   ,min(s_zip)   ,min(ss_ticket_number)   ,min(ss_sold_date_sk)   ,min(sr_returned_date_sk)   ,min(ss_item_sk)   ,min(d1.d_date_sk) from    store_sales   ,store_returns   ,store   ,date_dim d1   ,date_dim d2 where     d2.d_moy = 8 and ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number and ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk and ss_sold_date_sk   = d1.d_date_sk and sr_returned_date_sk   = d2.d_date_sk and ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk and ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and sr_store_sk = s_store_sk and d1.d_date between (d2.d_date - interval '120' day)                and d2.d_date and d1.d_dow = 2 and s_state in ('GA','IL','OH')  ;
rewritten_query:
WITH valid_dates AS (
    SELECT d2.d_date_sk AS return_date_sk,
           d1.d_date_sk AS sold_date_sk
    FROM date_dim d2
    JOIN date_dim d1
      ON d1.d_date BETWEEN (d2.d_date - INTERVAL '120' DAY) AND d2.d_date
     AND d1.d_year = d2.d_year
     AND d1.d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 8
    WHERE d2.d_moy = 8
      AND d1.d_dow = 2
)
SELECT MIN(s.s_store_name),
       MIN(s.s_company_id),
       MIN(s.s_street_number),
       MIN(s.s_street_name),
       MIN(s.s_suite_number),
       MIN(s.s_city),
       MIN(s.s_zip),
       MIN(ss.ss_ticket_number),
       MIN(ss.ss_sold_date_sk),
       MIN(sr.sr_returned_date_sk),
       MIN(ss.ss_item_sk),
       MIN(vd.sold_date_sk)
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN store_returns sr
  ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
 AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
 AND ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
 AND ss.ss_store_sk = sr.sr_store_sk
JOIN store s
  ON ss.ss_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
 AND sr.sr_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
JOIN valid_dates vd
  ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = vd.sold_date_sk
 AND sr.sr_returned_date_sk = vd.return_date_sk
WHERE s.s_state IN ('GA','IL','OH');

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Convert implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI JOINs so the join order is well-defined and the planner can choose hash joins on the fact tables.

Precompute the valid (sold_date_sk, return_date_sk) pairs in a CTE (`valid_dates`) so the d1/d2 date-range join is done once on the small date_dim table, then join both facts directly to the pair, eliminating the late range filter after the large fact joins.

Add implied predicates d1.d_year = d2.d_year and d1.d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 8: since d2 is always in August and d1 is within 120 days before d2, d1 must be in the same year and its month must be April–August. These are logically implied by the range condition and shrink the date-pair set.
Remove the redundant re-join to date_dim d1 in the main query; MIN(d1.d_date_sk) equals MIN(ss_sold_date_sk), which is carried by valid_dates.sold_date_sk, avoiding an extra dimension join.
No literal constants to fold beyond the interval; the derived d1 month/year bounds are the constant-folding benefits applied to the date-range join.
